properties.name: The multi-session section was restructured from an explanation into a four-step recipe anyone can follow, on Anthony's ask ("simple instructions so anybody can set it up"). No design element changed — cap:shared-sessions and cap:remote-sessions are exactly as built, and the why-it-works prose is kept below the steps rather than in front of them. Two things the old version did not say, both found by walking the setup on a real machine rather than from the code: (1) the sessions you already have EACH LAUNCH THEIR OWN reflow2 and one is holding the graph, so the server will not start until they are switched over — the first thing anyone hits, and it presents as a confusing lock error rather than as a missing step; (2) an SSH TUNNEL needs no --http-allow-host at all, because the far end then dials its own localhost, which the default allowlist already trusts — the simplest and most private route, and it was not documented anywhere.
